00-promise.question: Both drivers have tapped Reserve. Which observation would prove the service broke its promise?
00-promise.hint: A tap asks for a space. Which observation would show that both drivers actually own it?
00-promise.why: Two active grants for the same space prove a double booking. Two requests tell us only that there were two contenders.
00-promise.bridge: Two phones can ask for the same space. How many such requests could arrive in the busiest ten minutes?

01-demand.question: One fifth of 1.2 million reads arrive in ten minutes. What is the average arrival rate within that window?
01-demand.hint: First count the 240,000 reads in the burst. How many seconds are in the burst itself?
01-demand.why: 240,000 divided by 600 gives 400 reads per second. Dividing by a day would hide the burst.
01-demand.bridge: Suppose the peak needs two service instances. Which one is allowed to grant the last space?

02-write-boundary.question: Handler A has stopped after commit. Where can B discover the outcome?
02-write-boundary.hint: B starts with its own memory. Follow grant 17 to the component that recorded it.
02-write-boundary.why: B can retrieve grant 17 from the shared store even though the first reply was lost.
02-write-boundary.bridge: Sharing one database gives both handlers a place to write. What keeps both from claiming the last space?

03-conditional-write.question: When Ada's selected decision takes effect, how many inventory rows can Ben's update change?
03-conditional-write.hint: The selected decision is commit. Start from one space and keep Ada’s decrement before testing for a positive count.
03-conditional-write.why: Ada commits a free count of zero. Ben rechecks the row, finds no free space and changes zero rows.
03-conditional-write.bridge: One grant survives. What should the phone send if the winning confirmation never arrives?

changed.hint: The selected decision is rollback. Undo Ada’s decrement first. What number does Ben test now?
changed.why: Ada rolls back. The free count returns to one. Ben’s condition matches and his update changes one row.

04-retry-identity.question: The phone lost the reply for intention 17. Which number should it send now?
04-retry-identity.hint: A new number looks like a second deliberate tap. Which number can find grant 301?
04-retry-identity.why: Reusing 17 lets the service return its stored result without granting a second space.
04-retry-identity.bridge: The driver can retrieve one receipt. How can the app page through many receipts while new ones arrive?

05-history.question: The last pair shown was (10:00, 8). A newer row arrives. Which ID follows that pair?
05-history.hint: Keep the saved boundary fixed even though the list above it has moved.
05-history.why: ID 7 comes after the saved time-and-ID pair. Skipping two live rows repeats ID 8.
05-history.bridge: History can move between reads. How old can the map reading be by the time the driver sees it?

06-freshness.question: The source observed the lot at 92. At 115, how old is the answer?
06-freshness.hint: The cache received it at 100, but the underlying observation was already eight seconds old.
06-freshness.why: The source observation is 23 seconds old. Seven seconds of the allowance remain.
06-freshness.bridge: A map can lag a booking. How does the system remember to announce the booking if its process dies?

07-outbox.question: The first delivery of event 41 already changed the dashboard. What should a second delivery do?
07-outbox.hint: Look at the identity remembered beside the count. What new fact does a repeated 41 carry?
07-outbox.why: The repeated delivery adds no new grant. Record identity and effect in the same transaction.
07-outbox.bridge: A retry can be safe for the data. What happens when retries still consume scarce processing capacity?

08-overload.question: After the burst, 80 new requests arrive each second and 100 can finish. How quickly can old work drain?
08-overload.hint: Some of the 100 completions are already needed for the 80 new arrivals.
08-overload.why: Only 20 completions per second are spare, so 1,200 queued requests need 60 seconds.
08-overload.bridge: If one owner stays busy, can splitting data across more owners actually divide its work?

09-partitioning.question: West has spent its five local rights. Can it grant a sixth space using an unused east right without a transfer?
09-partitioning.hint: A right can be available somewhere without being spendable by this owner.
09-partitioning.why: West must refuse or acquire a right through a safe transfer. It cannot spend east's right independently.
09-partitioning.bridge: Local rights work without a remote vote. What if the design instead needs one shared decision during a split?

10-consensus.question: A and B have committed grant 17. Now A is isolated. Can A confirm another shared grant alone?
10-consensus.hint: Being the last known leader does not give A another vote.
10-consensus.why: A cannot commit a new shared grant alone. The pair may elect an eligible leader.
10-consensus.bridge: A booking is one decision. What changes when a separate payment provider controls the charge?

11-payment.question: Ada's hold expired and someone else owns the seat. Which durable record should the late charge create?
options: A new claim on the seat
11-payment.hint: The charge proves that money moved. Does it restore the expired right to the seat?
11-payment.why: Record refund work against this charge and preserve the current holder's seat.
11-payment.bridge: The charge can be correct and still be late. Where did the request spend its time?

12-diagnosis.question: The request waited 920 ms for a connection and spent 12 ms in its query. What could a free query save on this trace?
12-diagnosis.hint: Keep the earlier wait fixed. Which interval does faster query execution remove?
12-diagnosis.why: Only the 12 ms execution interval disappears. The wait still needs a separate diagnosis.
12-diagnosis.bridge: A trace helps diagnose delay. How would you verify the right data survived a restore?

13-recovery.question: A backup contains 10; then 20 is inserted, deleted, and 30 inserted. Which IDs exist immediately before the deletion?
13-recovery.hint: Stop replay at the target point. Which later writes have not happened yet?
13-recovery.why: 10 and 20 exist at that point. Receipt 30 needs separate reconciliation with the later history.
13-recovery.bridge: You can test a restore. How do you challenge a design when a reviewer changes the workload itself?

14-design-review.question: One post needs two million feed entries. At 50,000 entries/s, can more queue space meet a 10-second visibility target?
options: No, the writes take at least 40 s
14-design-review.hint: A queued entry is not yet visible. Count how many entries the writer can finish in ten seconds.
14-design-review.why: At most 500,000 entries finish in ten seconds. The design must change the work or its capacity.
14-design-review.bridge: Now hold total capacity fixed. Can changing only the assignment of individual reads cut a driver's wait?

15-routing.question: At time 10, worker A still has its first job and B has just finished. Which can start read three immediately?
15-routing.hint: Look for the bar that ends at time 10. Its worker has become available.
15-routing.why: B can start immediately. Change the policy to see whether the dispatcher actually sends the read there.
15-routing.bridge: Choosing a worker can reduce waiting. What if two reads on that worker ask storage the very same question?

16-coalescing.question: Two west requests already share a pending lookup. Can the arriving east caller reuse that result?
options: No, because it needs another lot
16-coalescing.hint: The key identifies the answer the caller is allowed to receive. Which lot is the pending result for?
16-coalescing.why: East starts its own lookup. This burst has three callers and two storage reads.
16-coalescing.bridge: Sharing a request also shares its failure. How can callers give a failing dependency time to recover?

17-circuit-breaker.question: A recovery probe entered at 110 and is still unanswered at 111. Should a second caller reach storage?
options: No, the probe slot is taken
17-circuit-breaker.hint: The quiet interval has ended, but how many simultaneous trial calls does this policy permit?
17-circuit-breaker.why: The single probe is in flight. Its reply decides whether subsequent calls pass.
17-circuit-breaker.bridge: A missed deadline can release a caller. What if a second driver still needs the underlying read?

18-waiter-deadlines.question: Ada's wait has expired. Ben's deadline has not. Storage now returns the west map. Which reply can Ben still receive?
options: Only the same timeout as Ada
18-waiter-deadlines.hint: Look at the line that ended at the cross. Is it Ben's wait, Ada's wait, or the underlying read?
18-waiter-deadlines.why: Ben can still receive the reading because his own wait and the shared work were both still active.
18-waiter-deadlines.bridge: In the final project, decide which caller may stop waiting, which operation continues and what evidence the next attempt must consult.
